passages.text: But perhaps one of you has thought that someone can be made into something else by another, but cannot himself transform himself into whatever he wishes, and that changing belongs to one who grows old and has to die .....; but this should not be thought of immortals. For did not angels, ageless ...... and of fiery substance, change into flesh, and those with Abraham who were ..........., whose feet people washed as though those beings were humans of the same substance? An angel also wrestled with Jacob, who was a human, turning into flesh so that he could come into bodily contact with him. And, having wrestled, he likewise turned back to his own nature when he wished. Having now changed into fire, he did not burn Jacob's broad tendon, but inflamed it and made him lame. One who cannot become something else when he wishes is mortal, being subject to his own nature. But one who can become what he wishes when he wishes, mastering nature itself and returning to youth, is immortal. Therefore, all the more, God's power transforms the body's substance into whatever he wishes whenever he wishes, and brings forth something of the same substance with no transformation present, but not of equal power. For the one who brings it forth can also bring about its turning back toward himself into another substance. But the one brought forth, being also a child of the transformation from that one, cannot become anything else without the will of the one who brought it forth, unless that one wishes.

lexical_decisions.rationale: The infinitive with having is read as the prospect or necessity of dying in the context of aging and mortality. The five-dot gap remains a gap; no lost adverb, noun, or other completion is supplied. A capacity-to-die emphasis is a material alternative to has to die.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ οἱ παρὰ τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ........... σθέντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: and those with Abraham who were ...........
lexical_decisions.rationale: The eleven-dot gap conceals the participle's lexical stem. Only its surviving passive plural ending licenses generic were in the English; no specific action such as appearing, dining, or being received is restored. The Abraham phrase and the following feet-washing clause are both retained.
The supplied ὁμῶς is taken in its alike or likewise sense rather than silently normalized to the adversative accent ὅμως. A contextual nevertheless interpretation remains possible but is not imposed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ πλατὺ νεῦρον οὐκ ἔκαυσε μέν, ἔφλεξε δέ
lexical_decisions.chosen: he did not burn ... the broad tendon, but inflamed it
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both the broad tendon and the contrast between the two fire verbs are retained. Scorched is a material alternative for the second verb; inflamed makes the distinction intelligible without adding an otherwise unexpressed severing or consuming of the tendon.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁμοούσιον μὴ παρούσῃ τροπῇ προβάλλει, ἰσοδύναμον δὲ οὔ
lexical_decisions.chosen: brings forth something of the same substance with no transformation present, but not of equal power
lexical_decisions.rationale: Same substance and equal power are explicitly distinguished. The participial phrase states the absence of a present transformation; its exact relation to the bringing forth is left broad rather than expanded into a specific material mechanism.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁ μὲν προβάλλων καὶ εἰς ἑτέραν πάλιν οὐσίαν ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν τραπέντα δύναται
lexical_decisions.chosen: the one who brings it forth can also bring about its turning back toward himself into another substance
lexical_decisions.rationale: The ability verb is elliptical, with the surrounding transformation account supplying the action and the accusative participle supplying the thing turned. The main text reads the turn as belonging to the brought-forth thing, with back toward himself referring to its producer. A material alternative understands the producer's own return to another substance through a loose shift of construction; the accusative participle more directly supports the object-oriented main reading. No specific additional power or physical procedure is supplied.

source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints five dots. The English preserves exactly five dots, without recovering or supplying the unavailable content.
The selected edition prints six dots after the ageless expression. The English preserves exactly six dots and translates the surviving fiery-substance description, without restoring the missing link.

The selected edition prints eleven dots followed by the surviving ending σθέντες. The English preserves exactly eleven dots, with only generic passive were representing the surviving inflection. The ending's unavailable lexical stem is not restored, and no complete original wording is claimed.

passages.text: While Peter was discussing these things, one of the advance party came in from Antioch ........... and said to Peter, ‘I want you to know, my lord, that Simon, publicly performing many wonders in Antioch and calling you a magician and a sorcerer, has stirred them to such hatred that every person staying there is himself eager to taste your flesh. So we of the advance party, together with our brothers whom you had planted with Simon, saw the city fiercely growling against you. We secretly assembled in one place and considered what we ought to do. While we were at a loss, Cornelius the centurion arrived, sent by Caesar to the governor of the province, whom the Lord had healed in Caesarea when he was possessed by a demon. We secretly summoned him, told him the reason for our discouragement, and asked for his help. He most eagerly promised to frighten Simon into flight, provided we assisted his undertaking. When we readily promised to do everything, he said, “While I make inquiries in secret through many friends, saying that I have come to arrest him and am seeking him because Caesar, having put many magicians to death and learned about him, sent me to seek him so that he might punish him like the magicians before him, let your people who are with him also report it, as though they had secretly heard somewhere that I have been sent to arrest him. Perhaps, when he hears, he will become afraid and flee.” Since, then, we thought of doing something else, it nevertheless happened in this way. For, having heard from many outsiders who showed him great favor and told him privately, and also from our planted people inside, and having received advice as though from his own people, he decided to withdraw. So, fleeing Antioch with Athenodorus, he has come here, as we have heard. That is why we advise you not yet to enter that city, until we know whether, in his absence, they will be able to subside from his slander against you.’

lexical_decisions.rationale: The people have gone ahead to Antioch and report back; the rendering identifies their forward role without assigning a military rank or an unexpressed organizational title.

lexical_decisions.chosen: is himself eager to taste your flesh
lexical_decisions.rationale: The tasting verb takes flesh as its genitive object, with your expressed at the end. The plural themselves is understood emphatically of the people rather than making their own flesh the food. The threat is retained as reported historical speech without embellishment.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸς τὸν τῆς ἐπαρχίας ἡγούμενον, ὃν ἐν Καισαρείᾳ δαιμονῶντα ἰάσατο ὁ κύριος
lexical_decisions.chosen: to the governor of the province, whom the Lord had healed in Caesarea when he was possessed by a demon
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main relative follows the nearest antecedent, the provincial governor. Cornelius is a material alternative antecedent from the preceding clause. The source does not resolve the reference by a repeated name, and no correction based on a familiar external healing account is supplied.

The phrase continues the account of brothers placed among Simon's associates. Planted people preserves their concealed placement rather than treating them as demons or as allies openly commissioned by Simon.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ἕτερόν τι ποιεῖν ἐπενοήσαμεν, ὅμως οὕτως ἐγένετο
lexical_decisions.chosen: Since, then, we thought of doing something else, it nevertheless happened in this way
lexical_decisions.rationale: The opening causal since and the subsequent nevertheless are retained despite the awkward connection. A contextual concessive alternative is although we considered doing something else, this nevertheless happened. The main text does not silently remove the other plan or claim they implemented it.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς κατὰ σοῦ διαβολῆς ἐκείνου ἀπόντος ὑπολῆσαι δυνήσονται
lexical_decisions.chosen: in his absence, they will be able to subside from his slander against you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The cessation reading is contextual, based on the question whether hostility will diminish after Simon's departure. The unusual supplied infinitive is not silently changed to another Greek form. See the blocking source issue: this proposed meaning remains unestablished rather than certified as a complete translation.

source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints eleven dots between Antioch and saying. The English retains exactly eleven dots and does not restore the missing content.

The supplied infinitive's lexical analysis and the cessation sense proposed in the English have not been established. The draft's subside is a contextual candidate only; without a defensible documented analysis it cannot be certified as translating this word. No unprinted normalized verb has been substituted. This uncertainty requires source-level or scholarly resolution before publication.
